title: Customers Who Bought Both Online and In-Store
description:
Find customers who have made purchases through **both** the online channel and the in-store channel using INTERSECT.

**Table: online_purchases** — `customer_id`, `amount`

**Table: instore_purchases** — `customer_id`, `amount`

Output column: `customer_id`. Order by `customer_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE online_purchases (customer_id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO online_purchases VALUES (101,50.00),(102,120.00),(103,85.00),(104,200.00),(105,60.00); CREATE TABLE instore_purchases (customer_id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO instore_purchases VALUES (102,45.00),(103,300.00),(106,90.00),(107,150.00),(104,75.00);
solution_sql: SELECT customer_id FROM online_purchases INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM instore_purchases ORDER BY customer_id

test_cases.description: Customers 102, 103, and 104 appear in both tables; 3 rows returned

hints: INTERSECT returns only rows that appear in BOTH queries — it automatically deduplicates the result.
Both SELECT statements must have the same number of columns with compatible data types.
explanation: INTERSECT returns customer_ids present in both online_purchases and instore_purchases. Online customers: 101, 102, 103, 104, 105. In-store customers: 102, 103, 104, 106, 107. Intersection: 102, 103, 104 — 3 rows. Customers 101 and 105 only bought online; 106 and 107 only bought in-store.
